accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 3
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The random-set limits assume tangent-cone regularity and continuously differentiable branch extensions at the specified boundary point.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The Fell and Hausdorff limits are claimed only under ass:tangent-cone-regularity and ass:branch-smoothness.

accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The decision problem is restricted to a singleton zeroth-order target and a fixed bounded tangent radius R.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Sections 4.2--4.3 and 5; Theorem 1 and Appendix D
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines diff-separation and diff-faithfulness, then proves that LDiffPC recovers the true difference-DAG skeleton and makes only sound orientations with perfect equality information.
Theorem 2 gives an asymptotic confidence set for one total causal effect as a union of explicit intervals over candidate DAG orderings, with a possible isolated zero.

The paper uses residual-bootstrap goodness-of-fit testing to form asymptotically valid causal-order confidence sets and explains post-processing them into causal-effect intervals under model uncertainty.
The resampling/screening procedure has asymptotic coverage for the fixed true causal effect, while oracle equivalence requires a strong nonzero-association condition.

Under Gaussian FCI and known outcome variance, the paper gives exact finite-sample coverage for a selected adjustment functional under its Markov-blanket condition, not unconditional coverage of this paired fixed direct-effect triple.
The paper studies identification of direct effects in linear difference graphs when the difference graph is supplied, including the BIRC3-to-PRKAR2B illustration.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add an explicit finite-dimensional enumeration algorithm for the p=3 collider fiber and one p=4 nontrivial boundary cell, including the resulting confidence union, to turn the semialgebraic representation into a reproducible computational object.

Sharpen Open-ended Question 1 into a local minimax lower-and-upper diameter frontier for a named subclass of branch cones, with a proposed least-favorable prior or invariance reduction as the starting route.
Add exact page/theorem anchors for the Strieder--Drton and Chang--Guo--Malinsky comparisons and state a numerical width comparison on a shared low-dimensional Gaussian benchmark.
